correctness.rationale: For a finite tree, independent bond connectivity yields \(M_v(p)=1+2S_v(p)/(n-1)\). Prüfer words exhaust all labeled trees with orders 2–7 (counts 1+3+16+125+1296+16807=18,248). For each tree, the included executed checker finds one vaccinee whose \(S_u-S_w\) has nonnegative coefficients in the degree-five Bernstein basis for every competitor; this proves the whole-continuum minimum. The eight-vertex distance polynomials are given term by term. Their comparisons reduce to \(S_3-S_0=p(1-p^2-p^3)\) and strict \(S_v>S_3\) for all other candidates, establishing the unique root and optima. For arbitrary \(n\ge8\), degree-three versus degree-at-most-two establishes center as uniquely optimal near \(p=0\); exact component-pair counts establish \(S_c(1)-S_b(1)=n-7>0\), hence its loss near \(p=1\). The actual packaged verifier ran successfully, with exact rational independent bond-state crosschecks. The finite checker is not invoked for infinite n.

originality.rationale: The novelty assessed is solely the exact tree-domain threshold: a parameter-independent optimum for every tree with at most seven vertices, explicit unique two-site switch at the eight-vertex spider at the root of \(p^3+p^2=1\), and examples for every \(n\ge8\). Bond-percolation epidemic interpretation and the mean pair-connectivity identity are known (Newman 2002). Node deletion and fragmentation objectives are known (Chen et al. 2006). Degree-versus-fragmentation tradeoffs and symbolic small-graph vaccination comparisons are known (Holme 2017), but that full article uses continuous-time infection/recovery dynamics and studies differences among objective classes; no proof of the current all-\(p\) seven-tree cutoff follows from it. The 2004 Holme heuristic work is a residual inaccessible full-text risk. An unindexed equivalent theorem or broader structural classification remains possible; a negative search is not uniqueness proof.
residual_risks: The complete text of Holme (2004) was inaccessible; an undisclosed equivalence or stronger theorem cannot be categorically excluded.
An unindexed mathematically equivalent distance-polynomial or vertex-susceptibility result could cover this sharp threshold without sharing its title or parameters.
The finite tree census is exact, but a future paper could prove a broader theorem from which this follows as a corollary; no priority certification is claimed.
Changing from the independent-bond model to continuous-time SIR with random infectious periods changes edge dependence and need not preserve the threshold.

value.rationale: Vaccinating exactly one node to minimize mean final outbreak size is a natural, published epidemic-control objective. A universally optimal choice would be robust to unknown transmissibility. The sharp tree order at which such robustness fails and the algebraic transition parameter for an explicit smallest witness supply a complete, motivated boundary classification and a general counterexample family. The result sharply distinguishes epidemic-control decisions from degree ranking and fragmentation alone, without asserting clinical significance outside its independent-bond model. It is not solely code reproduction, a coefficient identity, or an arbitrary numeric example.
